origin.description: Alias of stri_join_list. Concatenates the strings in each character vector of a list.

arguments.name: sep
arguments.text: A single string placed between the elements of each vector.

arguments.name: collapse
arguments.text: NULL, or a single string placed between the flattened vectors.

origin.details: stri_paste_list is the same function as stri_join_list and stri_c_list. Length-zero vectors are dropped, including NULL. If none remain, the result is an empty vector even when collapse is set. Each remaining vector is flattened with sep, using the default missing-value rule, so one missing element makes that result missing. collapse then joins those results, and a missing piece makes that one string missing. sep and collapse longer than one use the first element and warn. x must be a list; a character vector is rejected.
origin.value: A character vector with one string per remaining vector, or one string when collapse is set.

translation.description: Alias of stri_join_list. Concatenates the strings in each vector of a list.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: A list of vectors. A string element is a length-one vector. A nested list is one vector. None inside the list is dropped. A bare string is rejected.

arguments.name: sep
arguments.text: String placed inside each vector. NA makes each result missing.

arguments.name: collapse
arguments.text: None leaves one string per vector. A string joins those results.

translation.details: stri_paste_list is stri_join_list. Length-zero vectors are dropped, including NULL. If none remain, the result is an empty vector even when collapse is set. Each remaining vector is flattened with sep, using the default missing-value rule, so one missing element makes that result missing. collapse then joins those results, and a missing piece makes that one string missing. sep and collapse longer than one use the first element and warn. x must be a list; a character vector is rejected.
translation.value: A list of strings, or a one-element list when collapse is set.
translation.example:
from stringi._na import NA
from stringi.join import stri_paste_list
print(stri_paste_list([["a", "b"], [], ["c", NA]], sep="-"))
